In ordinary electromagnetism,

\[
\nabla\cdot \mathbf B=0
\]

because there are no magnetic monopoles. If isolated magnetic charges exist, this equation becomes nonzero, proportional to the magnetic charge density. Moving magnetic charges also produce a magnetic current, requiring an extra term in Faraday’s law, which describes the circulation (curl) of the electric field.

Thus the changed equations are the divergence of the magnetic field and the circulation of the electric field.

Answer: B
